messages:
leah (product): Quick sync write-up from customers + engineering: we need a clean contract for the embeddings ingest path (sync & async), backpressure semantics, billing for large dims, and a clear migration story. Customers asked for 4096 dims for nightly ETL and a fast 1-vector path for search.

omar (eng-ml): TL;DR on perf: single-vector latency grows roughly linearly with dims; memory grows more than linearly with batch dims due to KV cache. Measured on p4d: 2048 single 95p ~ 60ms; 4096 single 95p ~ 170ms. Bulk ingest (>=512 vectors) with 4096 -> need async ingest or quantized model.

tess (eng-platform): From API perspective propose two routes: 1) /v1/embeddings (sync) — for up to 64 vectors at 2048 dims (low-latency). 2) /v1/embeddings:async (async ingest) — accept large batches (<= 100k vectors) but returns job id and 202. Use signed callback/webhook or poll. Backpressure headers: X-Queue-ETA and X-Request-Quota-Used.

diego (infra): Autoscale notes: async ingestion will need a queue sharding strategy and a soft SLA. For Dedicated we can reserve high-memory nodes for 4096 jobs. For hosted, we should gate 4096 behind Dedicated or very small sync windows. Also recommend a per-customer concurrency cap and an adaptive admission controller.

yana (sales): A few enterprise customers will accept async ingest but want deterministic window (eg: finish within 4 hours). They also want a preview mode: upload a sample of batch (first 1000 vectors) to validate dims/format and get an ETA. This helps them pipeline integration.

leah (product): Proposed API contract (minimal, backwards-compatible):

Sync request example:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "model": "redwood-embed-1", "inputs": [[...], [...]], "compress_to": 2048 }
```
Sync limits: max_inputs=64 for dims<=2048. If client requests dims>2048 return 400 with guidance or 4096-only header.

Async request example:
```
POST /v1/embeddings?async=true
{ "model": "redwood-embed-large-4096", "inputs": [[...], ...], "callback_url": "https://..." }
```
Response: 202 Accepted + body {"job_id":"ingest_abc123","estimated_finish":"2024-06-05T02:00Z"} and headers X-Queue-ETA.

omar (eng-ml): Model fallback rules: if client omits model but requests dims=4096 -> if in Dedicated, route to large model; if hosted and not allowed, return 400 with suggestion: either request async ingest or set "compress_to":2048. Also add header X-Embeddings-Downsampled: true when server-side compression occurs.

tess (eng-platform): Error examples I will include in contract: 400 for unsupported dims (example payload), 413 for too large single sync request, 202 for async accepted. Also support 409 Conflict when customer exceeded concurrent ingest quota. Example 400: `{ "error":"unsupported_dimensions","message":"Requested 4096 dims not available on hosted; use Dedicated or async ingest." }`

yana (sales): Pricing ask: can we have a clear per-vector cost multiplier for dims>2048 (eg x1.8) and a premium for async priority processing? That will help enterprise finance signoffs.

diego (infra): Runbooks: need SLA tiers for async jobs (standard 0-12h, expedited <2h). Will add circuit-breaker for memory OOM and a retry policy for transient failures. Also need visibility: per-job logs and ETA recalculation.

leah (product): Launch criteria: 1) API spec + SDK changes (client-side helper to handle 202 job polling & callbacks), 2) perf matrix published for dims x batch sizes, 3) pricing signal for >2048 dims, 4) one Dedicated pilot (4096 nightly ingest) and two hosted pilots (high-volume 2048 async).

omar (eng-ml): Quick note: add a "preview" endpoint for customers to upload first 1000 vectors quickly and get validation + sample embeddings — will save support time.

tess (eng-platform): I'll draft the OpenAPI contract this week and include examples for sync/async/downsample, plus guidance for SDKs on polling and webhooks.

yana (sales): I'll collect pilot commitments and FAST-track two customers for QA.

deploy-bot: feature/embeddings-ingest-contract -> staging scheduled 2024-05-29T09:00Z (dry-run).

leah (product): Thanks team. Next check-in Wed to review OpenAPI draft and perf numbers. If anyone sees an unresolved blocker ping me.
